topic: Silent Embedding Drift Corrupts Production RAG
postText:
AI pipeline threw zero HTTP 500s, yet our clinical RAG assistant suddenly retrieved irrelevant protocols.
Culprit was not the LLM. It was silent embedding drift.

At the hospital where I work, we upgraded our embedding model for semantic search. New docs indexed with the new model, while legacy docs stayed on the old one in the same collection.

Same dimensions, incompatible latent spaces. Cosine similarity still returned scores, feeding garbage context to the LLM. In healthcare IT, silent context corruption is worse than downtime.

Treat vector space like strict DB schema. Three rules protect production RAG:

1. Version vector collections. Namespace indexes by model ID and chunking hash. Never mix vector spaces.
2. Shadow dual-index upgrades. Backfill a parallel collection asynchronously, then swap read aliases atomically.
3. Gate on retrieval recall. Run golden-dataset Recall@K checks in CI before flipping production traffic.

How does your team manage zero-downtime vector re-indexing when upgrading embedding models?
